alyssa: ran an nsys trace on the 13B cold-start regression this morning. timeline shows a cluster of GEMM kernels switching from cublasLt algos to slower cuBLAS fallback around 200ms into the request. attaching the key snippets below. :eyes:

alyssa: nsys command I used:
```bash
nsys profile -o trace_13b --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --trace=cuda,cublas --stats=true \
  --capture-start=cudaProfilerStart --capture-stop=cudaProfilerStop --duration=30 python perf_test.py --model 13B --batch 1
```

sam: can you paste the kernel timeline text or the cublas logs? curious which algo ids changed.

alyssa: pasted nvprof/cublasLt log fragment from the trace (trimmed):
```
[cuBLASLt] matmul id=0x7f8e1a algo=11 workspace=0 B, time=0.48ms
[cuBLAS]   matmul id=0x7f8e1b algo=fallback workspace=0 B, time=1.65ms
[cuBLASLt] matmul id=0x7f8e1c algo=3  workspace=128KB, time=0.52ms
[cuBLAS]   matmul id=0x7f8e1d algo=fallback workspace=0 B, time=2.10ms
```
Looks like for specific matmul shapes (seq_len=1024 KV concat), cublasLt picks algo with non-zero workspace but later requests seem to run with workspace=0 and are slower.

perf-bot: Regression alert: 2024-04-05T09:21Z p99 latency +7% vs baseline (canary run). See job perf/canary/13b/2024-04-05.

devon: probable two causes: (1) workspace allocation failing under memory pressure -> falling back to zero-workspace algos, (2) our kernel selection policy might be preferring deterministic (no-workspace) algos for safety. Did the trace show any cudaMalloc failures?

alyssa: yes there are intermittent cudaMalloc errors right before the fallback events in the full trace, e.g.:
```
E cudaMalloc 0x7f93... 0 bytes -> out of memory (allocated=6.1GB, free=128MB)
[cuBLASLt] fallback to non-workspace algo
```
I also re-ran with env var `CUBLASLT_ALGO_OVERRIDE=1` to force the high-perf algo and saw ~3% p99 improvement, but test OOMs at batch>1.

sam: ok that matches. two immediate experiments we can run: (A) run with a small persistent workspace pool so allocations don't require cudaMalloc per-call, (B) cap KV chunking to avoid peak shape that needs large workspace.

devon: also worth instrumenting matmul shape distribution in the router for a short window. if a tiny percentage of requests spike seq_len and cause workspace churn, adding a cheap ephemerally-compiled small-req path will avoid falling into the expensive code path.

alyssa: agree. plan I'm proposing:
- add short-lived metric: matmul_shape -> (m,k,n) histogram for 5m window (dev).
- implement a persistent workspace allocator in runtime (patch branch rtw/workspace-pool). initial pool size 1GB, LRU free.
- add canary flag to prefer deterministic/zero-workspace algos for low-memory instances and allow cublasLt override via runtime config.

sam: sounds good. owners? alyssa -> workspace pool + traces, devon -> router shape histogram + batching heuristic tweak, I'll add a test harness for persistent pool vs cudaMalloc to measure p99. I'll file tasks. :thumbsup:

alyssa: filing the issue now with trace links and nvprof output. attaching a perf snippet in the ticket. thanks all.
